topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture's place in the cancer course and states what students should learn.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of genetic susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as the evolution of mutation-bearing cells whose growth depends on their biological context.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and their interpretation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures influence cancer risk despite the roles of chance and inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections contribute to carcinogenesis, using Burkitt lymphoma to develop the interaction between infection and cellular mutation.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures damage DNA through mechanisms shaped by their chemical properties and cellular processing.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutation alone may be insufficient for cancer and show how promoter activity enables initiated cells to grow.

topics.label: Developmental and tissue susceptibility within carcinogenic mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics place tissue and life-stage susceptibility within the broader account of carcinogenesis and consolidate that account.

topics.label: Evidence and tests for carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence can connect exposures to cancer while explaining the limitations of methods used to establish carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions and framing their implications for everyday risk–benefit decisions.
